question.problem: The pressure $P$ of a gas kept at a fixed temperature varies inversely with the volume $V$ it occupies. When $V=2\,{\text{m}}^{3}$, the pressure is $P=1$ megapascal ($\text{MPa}$). Find the pressure when $V=0.5\,{\text{m}}^{3}.$
question.worked_solution:
The pressure $P$ is inversely proportional to the volume $V,$ so we have

$$
P=\frac{k}{V},
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that when the volume is $V=2\,{\text{m}}^{3},$ the pressure is $P=1$ megapascal ($\text{MPa}$). We can use this information to solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =\frac{k}{2} \\ 2\cdot 1 & =k \\ 2 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

We now have the equation

$$
P=\frac{2}{V}.
$$

We can use this equation to find the pressure when the volume is $V=0.5\,{\text{m}}^{3},$ as follows:

$$
P=\frac{2}{0.5}=4
$$

Therefore, the pressure of the gas when $V=0.5\,{\text{m}}^{3}$ is $4\,\text{MPa}.$
